item.title: PostgreSQL Unique Constraint Behavior with NULL Values: Techniques for Implementation
item.description:
“PostgreSQL Unique Constraint Behavior with NULL Values: Techniques for Implementation”

How does one properly construct a unique constraint in PostgreSQL when dealing with composite keys where one or more columns permit NULL values, and the requirement is to treat multiple NULL entries in that column as duplicates? Standard SQL treats nulls as distinct, often leading to unexpected behavior when enforcing business rules requiring a unique pairing even when a component is absent (null).

item.title: Prevent Duplicate Database Entries: Enforcing Unique Usernames in SQL
item.description:
“Prevent Duplicate Database Entries: Enforcing Unique Usernames in SQL”

How can a developer strictly enforce that a username column in a database table retains only distinct values, preventing the insertion of duplicate entries, and subsequently handle the resultant errors in application code?

The paramount technique for ensuring data integrity regarding unique identifiers like usernames lies at the database schema level. Subsequent application-layer checks serve as secondary defenses or for providing more user-friendly feedback.
